d001.note: At 5000 dpi there are two separate marks over المنزلة: a sukun crossed by a fatha over the lam (sukun on lam, fatha on mim), and a lone sukun (same size as a plain sukun) over the nun. So الْمَنْزِلَةِ with sukun on the nun.

d012.note: At 2600 dpi the kasra sits under the ha body and the sukun circle over the mim loop. The geometry matches حَمْلًا on the same page (ha vowel over the ha head, mim sukun over the mim), so the print has وَاحِمْلْنِي, a print error kept as printed (B's harakat). The parentheses are regular weight and stay outside the bold.

d015.note: At 2000 dpi the ra carries shadda+fatha and the ba only a plain fatha, with no shadda. So the print has الرَّبَانِيَّةِ, a print error kept (B's reading). The parentheses are regular weight and stay outside the bold (A).

d016.note: At 500 and 1000 dpi the ornament ﴾ touches «[البقرة» and «].(وَاقْذِفْ» is set closed up with no word space, so it stays glued as printed. No waqf sign is printed after ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ. The parentheses are regular weight and outside the bold.

d017.note: At 1000 dpi the comma to ornament gap is 49 px. The spaced «]، ﴿مَّآ» on p.063 measures 93 px, and the glued «]،﴿» kept in b15 measured about 42 px. So no word space is printed: «]،﴿وَمَا» is kept glued.

d022.note: Component analysis at 1000 dpi and a zoom at 4000 dpi show only ONE kasra in this word. It is centred under the final heh (kasra cx 226, heh portion ~203-250), not under the ta, whose dots are at cx 268. In the same footnote font the kasra of a ta sits exactly under its dots (بذاتِ: dots cx 347, kasra cx 348), and medial letters carry their own marks (عَطَّلَهَا). So the print has وصفاتهِ. Neither A (kasra on ta) nor B (two kasras) matches.

d023.note: At 800 dpi (components) the fatha (x 451-482) sits over the head of the waw of ومن (x 413-462), not over the dal of كاليهود (x 491-527). So the print has وَمن.

d026.note: At 1500 dpi the ornament ﴾ touches the bracket in «نَّفْسِكَ﴾[النساء» (about 35 px against about 105 px for the spaced «﴾ [النجم: ٤٢]»), so it is kept glued as printed. No waqf sign is printed after نَّفْسِكَ. The parentheses are regular weight and outside the bold.

d030.note: At 1500 dpi the flower of ﴾ touches the bracket of «[الشورى» (about 40 px, glued), so A's «أَمْرِنَا﴾[الشورى:» is kept. No waqf sign is printed after أَمْرِنَا.

d033.note: At 2400 dpi a kasra is printed low under the heh of the bold الله ligature, between the two footnote lines and clearly above «(٢) البخاري». It is the same low placement as the kasra of بِاللهِ adjudicated in b15. So the print has اللهِ.

d035.note: At 2000 dpi only ONE kasra is printed under the lam-mim-ya ligature (component cx 291, under the lam foot, with the mim loop at about 175-265). In this ligature a lam kasra and a mim kasra fall in the same place, as noted in b27 d019 for the same word. It cannot be assigned with certainty, so A's [؟:عَوَالمِي] marker is kept as in b27. The parentheses are regular weight and outside the bold.

d037.note: At 1500 dpi the flower of ﴾ is about 30 px from the bracket of «[آل عمران: ٨١]» (glued; the spaced control is about 105 px), so it is kept glued as printed. No waqf sign is printed after وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥ.

q001.note: No waqf sign is printed after the last word of the quotation before the closing ornament (zoom at 900 dpi; the only coloured signs on these pages are ۚ in 12:108 and ۖ in 42:11). The quote ends there, so this is a genuine print variant, as in b15/b17. (ٱتَّبَعَنِى, 12:108)

q003.note: The footnote verse is set in bold naskh, not the mushaf font. At 1600 dpi there is no silent-zero sign over the final alif of تُوَلُّوا, so the print is kept as printed (a genuine print variant).
